Unlike modern CPUs like the Intel i9, which has 24 cores, a modern GPU like the RTX 4090 has over 16,000 cores. A CPU is designed to be versatile, while a GPU is designed to go really fast and parallel. Kuda allows developers to tap into the GPU's power, and data scientists all around the world are using it this very moment, trying to train the most powerful machine learning models. It works like this. You write a function called a Kuda kernel that runs on the GPU. You then copy some data from your main RAM over to the GPU's memory, then the CPU will tell the GPU to execute that function or kernel in parallel. C equals A plus B, but because hypothetically we're doing billions of operations in parallel, we need to calculate the global index of the thread in the block that we're working on. From there, we can use Managed, which tells Kuda this data can be accessed from both the host CPU and the device GPU.
